Nested Conditions

Stage 3 Concept ⏱ 12 min 📖 Glossary

Real choices stack: inside “it rains” sits “have umbrella?”. Nest carefully — or flatten with &&.

🔎 Motivating questionWhen is a box inside a box clearer than two boxes side by side?

Objectives

  • Nest ifs safely
  • Flatten with &&
  • Trace nested paths

Needs first: if, else if, and else

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

Russian dolls: outer “weekend?” contains inner “sunny?”. Two levels fine; five dolls confuse — flatten into one checklist.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: dolls always fit. Nested ifs hide paths exponentially — 3 levels = 8 paths to test.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

Nesting = if inside if. Inner runs only if outer true.

Flatten when possible: if (a && b) beats two levels. Guard clauses return early.

Trace with a table: list outer/inner combos.

3 Watch it move: Dolls

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
boolean weekend = true;
boolean sunny = false;
if (weekend) {
  if (sunny) System.out.println("Picnic");
  else System.out.println("Museum");
} else {
  System.out.println("Work");
}
▶ Output Museum
  • Outer true → enter.
  • Inner false → Museum.
  • Else pairs with nearest if — use braces.
💡 Why this output?Weekend true, sunny false → inner else.

5 Interactive experiment

Change values, watch consequences. Simulation — honest, not a real compiler.

Try it (visual simulation — not a real compiler)
Weekend logic: try values.
…

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: Dangling else confusionWhy: else binds nearest if.
✅ Fix: Always brace nested ifs.
❌ Mistake 2: 5-deep nestingWhy: Untestable paths.
✅ Fix: Flatten with && or early return.
❌ Mistake 3: Checking inner before outer setWhy: Null/empty outer crashes.
✅ Fix: Outer validates first.

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Flatten it

Flatten: if (a) { if (b) { go(); } }

HintOne &&.
Solutionif (a && b) { go(); }
Count paths

2 nested ifs = how many paths?

Hint2 × 2.
Solution4: TT, TF, FT, FF (outer false skips inner).

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • Nesting = choice inside choice.
  • Flatten with && when you can.
  • Brace everything.
🧠 Recall challengeWhen is nesting justified vs &&?
